Around the Christmas period last year, two advent calendar series caught my attention: Athanasia Monika Mowinckel's ["Modern R Package Development"](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/drmowinckels_rpackageadvent2025-rstats-rpackageadvent2025-activity-7400837138604290048-dOt4/) and Digtial Research Academy's [Open Science Bird](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/digital-research-academy_were-launching-our-dradvent-calendar-featuring-activity-7399800562126352385-UTAj/). Inspired by these, I made an attempt to convert the content of these advent calendars into a scrollytelling format using Quarto.

## What is Scrollytelling?

Scrollytelling is a storytelling technique that combines narrative text with interactive visual elements, allowing readers to engage with the content as they scroll through a webpage. I used the [Closeread extension for Quarto](https://closeread.dev) to create the scrollytelling experience.

## The experiments

The scrollytelling versions of the advent calendars can be found here (best viewed on a laptop):

- [Modern R Package Development - Scrollytelling Version](https://saranjeetkaur.github.io/modern_r_pkg_dev/)
- [Open Science Bird - Scrollytelling Version](https://saranjeetkaur.github.io/opensci_bird/)
